1. Criminal Case No. : 5156/2019 2. Date of commission of offense : In the year 2009 3. Date of institution of the case : 04.04.2019 4. Name of the complainant : State 5. Name of accused and parentage : Sumit Yadav S/o Vijay Yadav
6. Offence complained of : 420/511/471 IPC 7. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty 8. Date on which order was reserved : 28.05.2025 9.
Final order : Convicted 10. Date of final order : 09.06.2025 1.
The accused is facing trial for offences u/s 420/511/471 IPC.

The genesis of the prosecution story is that in the year 2009 at unknown time at PHQ, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS IP Estate accused submitted form no. 17609 with forged DL No. 2590/MTR/03 allegedly issued from Transport Authority, Mathura, UP for the post of driver in FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs.
Sumit Yadav 1/16 Delhi Police and fraudulently and dishonestly induced the examining / appointing authority of Delhi Police to believe the same to be original / genuine and also on the abovesaid date,
time and place he used the forged DL No. 2590/MTR/03 as genuine which he knew or had reason to believe at that time that the same was forged and thus committed an offence u/s 420/468/471 IPC.
Pursuant to the complaint made by the complainant, the criminal law was set into motion vide registration of the FIR against accused.
The aforesaid person was however, never arrested by the police.
On completion of investigation, the present charge-sheet for offences u/s 420/468/471 IPC was filed against accused.

6. After prosecution evidence, the statement of accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded, wherein all the incriminating circumstances were offered to accused to which accused replied that he was falsely implicated in the matter.

He stated that he appeared and qualified the examination and in year 2003, he visited office of ARTO Mathura for issuance of DL where he met one agent at the gate of the authority and he offered his assistance for issuance of DL.
Accused trusted him and submitted his application to that person by adopting proper process.

He appeared for DL test and after following standard procedure he was told by the said agent to collect the DL after one month and accordingly accused collected his DL from the said agent and submitted the same alongwith his application.
Accused did not opt to lead evidence in his defence.
7. I have heard the contentions advanced by Ld. APP for the State and also by Ld. Defence counsel representing the accused.

8. Ld. APP for State has contended that the prosecution has proved its case beyond all reasonable doubts and therefore, the accused is liable to be convicted for offences u/s 420/511/471 IPC.
9.
Per contra, Ld. Defence counsel for accused has vehemently argued that the prosecution has failed to establish guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
He argued that the report on the basis of which FIR was registered, is not part of the record.

He further argued that SI Vivek FIR No.
251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 7/16 was not examined and report dated 18.05.2012 does not mentioned the name of accused.

He further argued that PW-8 has not proved the letter no.

With these submissions, prayer is made for acquittal of accused from the alleged offences.

10. Having discussed the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, the following issues emerge for our consideration:-
(i) Whether accused used the forged driving license despite knowing that it was false and fabricated and not genuine and used the same while applying for the vacancies and thus cheated the complainant.
Analysis:

The Hon'ble Supereme Court of India in Mariam Fasihuddin & Anr. Vs. State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr. Crl. Apeal no. 335/2024 observed The offence of cheating under Section 42 0 IPC:
10. Section 420 IPC provides that whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy, the whole or any part of valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be liable to be punished for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

sentences.text: Further, Section 415 IPC distinctly defines the term'cheating'.

The provision elucidates that an act marked by fraudulent or dishonest intentions will FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 8/16 be categorised as 'cheating' if it is intended to induce the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, causing damage or harm to that person.

entities.text: PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 8/16
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11.It is thus paramount that in order to attract the provisions of Section 420 IPC, the prosecution has to not only prove that the accused has cheated someone but also that by doing so, he has dishonestly induced the person who is cheated to deliver property.

There are, thus, three components of this offence, i.e., (I) the deception 10 P a g e of any person,
(ii) fraudulently or dishonestly inducing that person to deliver any property to any person, and (iii) mensrea or dishonest intention of the accused at the time of making the inducement.
There is no gainsaid that for the offence of cheating, fraudulent and dishonest intention must exist from the inception when the promise or representation was made.
12.It is well known that every deceitful act is not unlawful, just as not every unlawful act is deceitful.
Some acts may be termed both as unlawful as well as deceitful, and such acts alone will fall within the purview of Section 420 IPC.

It must also be State vs Sumit Yadav on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18828163/
5 understood that a statement of fact is deemed 'deceitful' when it is false, and is knowingly or recklessly made with the intent that it shall be acted upon by another person, resulting in damage or loss.2

'Cheating' therefore, generally involves a preceding deceitful act that dishonestly induces a person to deliver any FIR No.
251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 9/16 property or any part of a valuable security, prompting the induced person to undertake the said act, which they would not have done but for the inducement.

sentences.text: 13.Theterm 'property' employed in Section 420 IPC has a well defined connotation.
Every species of valuable right or interest that is subject to ownership and has an exchangeable value- is ordinarily understood as 'property'.
It also describes one's exclusive right to possess, use and dispose of a thing.

The IPC itself defines the term 2 P. Ramanatha Aiyar, Advanced Law Lexicon, 6th Edition, Vol. 1, pg.903. 11| P a g e 'moveable property' as, "intended to include corporeal property of every description, except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth."
Whereas immoveable property is generally understood to mean land, benefits arising out of land and things attached or permanently fastened to the earth.

The offence of forgery under Sections 468 and 471 IPC: 21.The offence of 'forgery' under Section 468 IPC postulates that whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic document forged, shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Whereas Section 471 IPC states that whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any documents which he knows or has FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 10/16 reason to believe it 15 | P a g e to be a forged document, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document.
22.There are two primary components that need to be fulfilled in order to establish the offence of 'forgery', namely: (I) that the accused has fabricated an instrument; and (ii) it was done with the intention that the forged document would be used for the purpose of cheating.

entities.text: PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav

sentences.text: Simply put, the offence of forgery requires the preparation of a false document with the dishonest intention of causing damage or injury.
23.The
offences of 'forgery' and 'cheating' intersect and converge, as the act of forgery is committed with the intent to deceive or cheat an individual.
Having extensively addressed the aspect of dishonest intent in the context of 'cheating' under Section 420 IPC, it stands established that no dishonest intent can be made out against the Appellants.
Our focus therefore will now be confined, for the sake of brevity, to the first element, i.e.,the preparation of a false document.

Considering the primary ingredient of dishonest intention itself could not be established against the Appellants, the offence of forgery too, has no legs to stand.

sentences.text: In such like situation and coupled with the nature of allegations, we are unable to appreciate as to why the Appellants be subjected to the ordeal of trial.

11. The case of prosecution as per original complaint Ex. PW7/A is that accused applied for the vacancies of Constable(driver) upon the strength of the heavy driving license no. 2590/MTR/03 issued from ARTO, Mathura but upon the verification, the DL was not found issued in name of accused from the Transport Authority Mathura.
In the trial, PW-7 complainant proved the original complaint Ex. PW7/A by identifying his signatures upon the complaint and affirming the version of complaint.

12. During the trial, the prosecution was required to prove the verification report bearing no.
1190/license satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012 and 1883/license satyapan/2012 dated 09.05.2018,
on the basis of which the charge-sheet was filed against accused.
Ex. PW2/A is verification report bearing no. 1190/license satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012 issued by the then ARTO Mathura.
As per the entry mentioned at S.No. 32, the license bearing no. 2590/MTR/03 was found issued in name of one Sh. Ram Babu S/o Vasudev.

Ex. PW3/A is verification report bearing no. 1883/license satyapan/2012 dated 09.05.2018 as per which it was remarked by the then ARTO, "jari nahi hai".
13. PW-3 Ms. Babita, the then ARTO, Mathura appeared to prove the verification report Ex. PW3/A.
The report further observes that the license was found fake after verification.

She testified that the DL NO.
FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 12/16 2590/MTR/03 was not found issued in the name of Sh. Sumit Yadav.
She duly identified her signatures upon the report.
In the cross-examination, no material contradiction could be deduced.
Ld. counsel for the accused argued that the letter on the basis of which Ms. Babita prepared Ex. PW3/A is not on record.
However, if that be so, it does not impeach the credibility of report Ex. PW3/A and that too when PW-3 herself deposed that DL verification report was sought by Delhi Police in year 2018.
She further affirmed in her cross-examination that she had personally checked the record.

In this regard, Ex. PW1/A(OSR)
is the original record on the basis of which the report Ex. PW3/A was prepared.
14. PW-1 Sh. Suraj Pal Singh, senior assistant, ARTO Mathura stepped into the witness box and brought the original DL issuing register of year 2003.

The relevant entry of the said register is Ex.
PW1/A(OSR) and as per entry in the original record, DL No. 2590/MTR/03 was issued in name of one Sh. Ram Babu S/o Sh. Vasudev R/o Beheta, Chhata, Mathura, UP.

When the original record reflects that the license bearing no. 2590/MTR/03 was issued to one Sh. Ram Babu and not to accused, the defence of accused that the original verification report dated 18.05.2018 has not been produced, is of no consequence.

Further, Ld. counsel for the accused put one GD dated 18.05.2016 State vs Sumit Yadav on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18828163/
7 registered at PS Mathura Refinery vide mark PW1/DA to PW-1 to which PW-1 admitted that one fire incident took place at the office of ARTO Mathura and some record was burned in the said incident but the original record pertaining to the present case has been made available by ARTO officials,
Mathura in the trial.
Therefore, accused cannot take any benefit of the fire incident happened at the office of ARTO, Mathura in year 2016.

15. It is not in dispute that accused applied for the vacancies and FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 13/16 appeared in the exam and submitted that DL bearing no.
2590/MTR/03 to the Delhi Police for the purpose of securing a Govt. job.

sentences.text:
When the original record reflects that the license no. 2590/MTR/03 was issued to some other person and not to the accused,
the argument that verification report dated 22.05.2012 does not make any difference.

Furthermore,
PW-7 complainant proved the original complaint Ex. PW7/A and Ex. PW7/A refers one report dated 22.05.2012.
However, the same appears to be a clerical error as the FIR was registered on the basis of verification report dated 18.05.2012 and not on the basis of any report dated 22.05.2012.
In this regard, Ld. counsel for the accused did not ask any question to PW-7 regarding the date of the report.
16. Another argument is that the verification report Ex. PW2/A dated 18.05.2012 does not mention the name of accused.
However, the careful perusal of the report reflects that at S.No. 32, the name of accused finds a mention stating that DL No. 2590/MTR/03 was issued to one Sh. Ram Babu and not to the accused.
Furthermore, accused in his statement u/s 313 Cr.PC admitted that he met one agent at the gate of the authority and he submitted his DL application through the said person by adopting proper process.

Meaning thereby, that accused did not fill the form directly to the ARTO office and he collected the DL from the said agent and the collection of DL from the agent is not the proper procedure of getting a Heavy Driving License.

17. Coming further, accused is a resident of Rewari, Haryana and as per section 9 of the MV Act,
1988, any person may apply for a driving license in a State in which he is ordinarily residing or carrying on his business or in which any school as mentioned in section 12 of the MV Act, 1988 is established.

No explanation has been given by the accused FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs.
Sumit Yadav 14/16 as to how and in what circumstances, he went to Mathura for getting his driving license prepared.

sentences.text: Court cannot lose the sight of the fact that accused is a resident of Haryana and there are already driving motor schools established in Haryana and Delhi(nearby to Rewari).
There was no reason for him to go to Mathura for preparation of the driving license.
It is not the case of accused that accused was gainfully employed in Mathura or was resident of Mathura at the relevant time when he got the aforestated license prepared.
18. Furthermore, Ex. PW2/A is the only verification report which could not be proved by the prosecution as its author has not appeared.
However, the verification report Ex. PW3/A has been duly proved by the prosecution which reflects that the license bearing no. 2590/MTR/03 was not issued to accused.
Additionally, the original record indicates that the license was issued to some other person.
Ld. counsel for the accused argued that the other person in whose name the license was found to be issued, has not been examined by prosecution.

However, when the original public record from a Govt. office has reflected that the license bearing no. 2590/MTR/03 was not issued to State vs Sumit Yadav on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18828163/
8 accused, there was no requirement to add another person as witness who does not know anything about the present case.
19. Defence could not brought any material contradiction in the cross-examination of the star witnesses i.e. PW-1 Suraj Pal Singh and PW-3 Ms. Babita Verma, both from ARTO, Mathura.
The suggestion given to PW-3 Ms. Babita was that she prepared the incorrect report at the instance of IO.

At the same time, Ld. counsel for the accused had tried to impeach that PW-3 prepared Ex.
PW3/A without receiving any communication from IO.

Further, another suggestion was given by Ld. FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 15/16 defence counsel that there was variation in the digit of number in the DL in question and the report Ex. PW3/A but the suggestion was denied by the witness and the careful perusal reflects that there is no variation in the number of DL anywhere.
20.

sentences.text: As an outcome of the discussion made above, this Court is of the view that the answers to the issue framed at S.No. (i) is in positive.

Prosecution has successfully proved its case beyond reasonable doubts that accused used the forged DL despite being aware that it was not genuine but since the accused was not finally selected for the post of Ct. (Driver), his act is only an attempt to cheat the complainant with an intention to cause wrongful loss to the complainant.

Accordingly,
accused Sumit Yadav is convicted for offences u/s 420 r/wDigitally 511/471 IPC.

After taking the cognizance of the offences, the provisions of section 207 Cr.P.C. were complied with by supplying copy of charge- sheet and documents to accused.
Thereafter, on the basis of material on record, charges for offences u/s 420/511 and 471 IPC were framed against accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
In order to establish the guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined 10 witnesses in all.

opennyai_summary.issue:
10. Having discussed the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, the following issues emerge for our consideration:-
(i) Whether accused used the forged driving license despite knowing that it was false and fabricated and not genuine and used the same while applying for the vacancies and thus cheated the complainant.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Supereme Court of India in Mariam Fasihuddin & Anr. Vs. State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr. Crl. Apeal no. 335/2024 observed The offence of cheating under Section 42 0 IPC:
10. Section 420 IPC provides that whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy, the whole or any part of valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be liable to be punished for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.
11.It is thus paramount that in order to attract the provisions of Section 420 IPC, the prosecution has to not only prove that the accused has cheated someone but also that by doing so, he has dishonestly induced the person who is cheated to deliver property.
There are, thus, three components of this offence, i.e., (I) the deception 10 P a g e of any person,
(ii) fraudulently or dishonestly inducing that person to deliver any property to any person, and (iii) mensrea or dishonest intention of the accused at the time of making the inducement.
There is no gainsaid that for the offence of cheating, fraudulent and dishonest intention must exist from the inception when the promise or representation was made.
12.It is well known that every deceitful act is not unlawful, just as not every unlawful act is deceitful.
Some acts may be termed both as unlawful as well as deceitful, and such acts alone will fall within the purview of Section 420 IPC.
Whereas Section 471 IPC states that whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any documents which he knows or has FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs. Sumit Yadav 10/16 reason to believe it 15 | P a g e to be a forged document, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document.
22.There are two primary components that need to be fulfilled in order to establish the offence of 'forgery', namely: (I) that the accused has fabricated an instrument; and (ii) it was done with the intention that the forged document would be used for the purpose of cheating.
Simply put, the offence of forgery requires the preparation of a false document with the dishonest intention of causing damage or injury.
offences of 'forgery' and 'cheating' intersect and converge, as the act of forgery is committed with the intent to deceive or cheat an individual.
Having extensively addressed the aspect of dishonest intent in the context of 'cheating' under Section 420 IPC, it stands established that no dishonest intent can be made out against the Appellants.
The determination of whether the Appellants prepared a false document, by forging Respondent No.
2's signature, however, cannot be even prima facie ascertained at this juncture.
Considering the primary ingredient of dishonest intention itself could not be established against the Appellants, the offence of forgery too, has no legs to stand.
In such like situation and coupled with the nature of allegations, we are unable to appreciate as to why the Appellants be subjected to the ordeal of trial.
Therefore, accused cannot take any benefit of the fire incident happened at the office of ARTO, Mathura in year 2016.
Meaning thereby, that accused did not fill the form directly to the ARTO office and he collected the DL from the said agent and the collection of DL from the agent is not the proper procedure of getting a Heavy Driving License.
17. Coming further, accused is a resident of Rewari, Haryana and as per section 9 of the MV Act,
1988, any person may apply for a driving license in a State in which he is ordinarily residing or carrying on his business or in which any school as mentioned in section 12 of the MV Act, 1988 is established.
No explanation has been given by the accused FIR No. 251/2013, PS IP Estate State Vs.
Sumit Yadav 14/16 as to how and in what circumstances, he went to Mathura for getting his driving license prepared.
Court cannot lose the sight of the fact that accused is a resident of Haryana and there are already driving motor schools established in Haryana and Delhi(nearby to Rewari).
There was no reason for him to go to Mathura for preparation of the driving license.
However, the verification report Ex. PW3/A has been duly proved by the prosecution which reflects that the license bearing no. 2590/MTR/03 was not issued to accused.
Prosecution has successfully proved its case beyond reasonable doubts that accused used the forged DL despite being aware that it was not genuine but since the accused was not finally selected for the post of Ct. (Driver), his act is only an attempt to cheat the complainant with an intention to cause wrongful loss to the complainant.

Accordingly,
accused Sumit Yadav is convicted for offences u/s 420 r/wDigitally 511/471 IPC.
